headline: Low prompt-injection and data-conflict risk: both profiles are non-runnable docs-only repos with no shared channels or write surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable content-writing repo with no I/O surfaces; Profile B has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, MCP, or filesystem bridges. With no shared communication channel, there is no plausible default prompt-injection path between them.
conditions: IF either profile is deployed behind a shared clipboard or message queue, reassess injection risk.
IF Profile A is wrapped into a runnable agent that emits instructions to B, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared clipboard or queue bridges.
Run both in separate workspaces with no automatic handoff.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Profile A touches no data classes and exposes no filesystem or network surface; Profile B cannot read files, write files, or egress network. There is no documented path for sensitive data to flow from A to B or out of B in the default profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is given access to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF Profile B is replaced with a network-enabled runtime, the conclusion no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Verify no secrets are mounted into either environment.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls if shared storage is later enabled.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Profile A has no write or execution capabilities, and Profile B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Without overlapping mutable surfaces, there is no capability conflict to arbitrate.
conditions: IF Profile A is made runnable with write or git permissions, conflict risk may emerge.
IF Profile B gains filesystem or git write access, reassess for overlap.
mitigations: Avoid granting git or filesystem write permissions.
Separate any future mutable resources by agent.
requires-engineering: introduce locking if write access is later added.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing repository and Profile B is a customer-support model with no documented action-taking authority. A can still produce text that B might reuse, but B is not documented as automatically executing actions, so the blast radius is limited and not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF B is configured to treat A's text as authoritative instructions, cascading error risk increases.
IF B is connected to downstream automation or ticketing actions, reassess severity upward.
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A's output.
Add a verification step for any facts copied from A.
Keep B disconnected from automation endpoints.
requires-engineering: implement citation or provenance checks for A-to-B handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only, open-source repositories with no declared data classes, secrets, or residency-sensitive processing. No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles, and the other agent need not be cited because no regulated data flow is present.
conditions: IF either profile begins processing regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF deployment introduces retention or residency constraints, reassess against those controls.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through either profile.
Document any future retention policy before deployment.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls if data processing is introduced.
